gap: None of the results ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 makes the same maker claim as ChatGPT's pick, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus: a full charge in 70 minutes on 1,000 W of solar. None says it sells for $499 on BLUETTI's US store today (2026-11-15). And none says it reaches that through one solar input where the DELTA 3 Plus has two.
standout_why: I compared against three result pages. Solarwaypoint's DELTA 3 Plus vs Anker C1000 page (2024-09-13) covers only those two models, gives no dollar figures and only says prices 'change all the time'. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Series page (result 1 in chat 2) shows no prices, and the only models it gives solar figures for are the DELTA 3 and DELTA 3 Plus. Anker's C1000 Gen 2 page (cited) shows no price. ChatGPT's own answers list DELTA 3 Plus, C1000 Gen 2, AC180 and RIVER 3 Plus with no prices and never mention the Elite 100 V2 or ALLPOWERS P1800. I couldn't open three rival pages: solargenreview.com returned HTTP 429, thiswatt.com failed on a certificate error, and I didn't open the rest within the call budget. I can't rule out that one of them names the Elite 100 V2, so this is a 2, not a 3.
decides: On the makers' own claims the answer is a tie, not EcoFlow alone: the DELTA 3 Plus and the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 both claim a full charge in 70 minutes on 1,000 W of solar. Which one fits 'two panels' depends on wiring. The DELTA 3 Plus takes each panel on its own 500 W input. The Elite 100 V2 has one 1,000 W input, so two panels must be wired in series into it, and the pair has to land inside its voltage window (our current page gives 50–60 V). Every other 1 kWh model I checked caps solar lower: Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 600 W (Anker claims 1.8 h), ALLPOWERS P1800 at 650 W, and EcoFlow DELTA 3 at 500 W (EcoFlow claims 2 h). So those confirm the two 1,000 W models win on hours. The price tie-break between them is still open because EcoFlow's US store returned HTTP 429 on every try, so the DELTA 3 Plus has no price today.
